# Oct 28 outer LPB | Channel 6-8

Was supped to take the neighbour with me but he cancelled late, so went solo. I was thinking of not posting because some other very good fishermen i.e., [@jammer](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/15/), [@SkinnyTiller](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/10003/), did not fair as well, but hey what is worst thing that could happen, I could be called a bullshidter? Been called worse.

Here we go, started just west of the Nanticoke pier at about 6:30 in 25fow. Not much on the screen, but at least there was some protection from the waves. Headed south dragging glow harnesses behind #10 jets. Finally saw some life around 35fow but still no hits. Brought in the baits to check them out and they were fowled with algae. Switch one to a UV storm deep thunderstick and got a good fish right away. Kept switching baits around from harnesses to cranks, to dipsys etc.

Hit a period for about 45 min where it was like the middle of August, hard to keep more than one rod in the water. Continued south and baits would get a few fish then go dead, change it out for another bait and it would catch, then go dead.

Went through a lot of water with few marks but still go the occasion fish. Fighting a good walleye and the other rod went off with a good run. Landed and released the walleye then landed a nice bull coho with a pretty good hook on it lower jaw.

It went on like that for most of the day. Periods of not much action, changing lures and presentation, then a flurry of action. Had another big silver bullet on, a worm harness behind a dipsy. Lots of line peeling and got most of the way to the boat, but when walleye fishing I don't use snubbers and a good headshake behind the boat set it free.

Had the three 22-25" walleye I wanted for the day but then another good fish wrapped a hook around its gill and came home for the ride as well. Fished 25-55fow. No real pattern for preferred depth. Speed was 1.8-2.2, with 1.8 best for harnesses but still a lot of hits on cranks at that speed. I have no idea how many I caught, no one would believe me anyway.

All females came home. The 2 that had full stomachs had shad between 2" and 5" long. I will try to get some pictures of the lures I used, but flicker minnows and flicker shad 100-125ft behind inline boards did very well. The boards beat the dipsys 5-1 and were hit when there was little or nothing on the screen. My guess is that the shallow fish are being pushed to the side by the boat and do not show up on the screen.

Glad you got out again ST....what a beauty day. I was wondering who all would get out as I drove to work. One thing for sure.....Not many days like this to be had for the end of October. Wow.

 

[![SkinnyTiller](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/10/10003.jpg?1754179816)](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/skinnytiller.10003/)

Lucked out with departure time from London, got to Hoovers and lake looked sweet. Launched 11:30 and just fired up the tiller when low-and-behold, here comes [@jammer](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/15/) up the channel- had a good chat and was off. Started shallow (25fow) with boards and cranks but the hooks on the sonar weren't interested in the new P10s/Bandits. Switched to Gibbs and modified RRF off Dipsys- Redfin hooked up 1st 45fow but lost it just before the boatflip. Went downhill SE to 54fow, made 3 E-W passes S of Shoal, pulled lines W of and headed E towards Peacock. Reset over 45fow, hooked into 2nd over 42fow on blue jointed Rapala.... that one only got halfway to the boat 🙄 Ran 20+ baits but nothing seemed to work so on a lark put out big, jointed floating Rapala off Dipsy 71 on 3, 10 mins later opened the bail, closed it at 83 and wham- nice 27" 7lb 6oz to the livewell. Fished til 6pm looking for it's twin but was very content to call it a day with the lake like glass and a splendid consolation on ice.

# Fishing Report - PORT GLASGOW- 2 Tillers in 1

[![SkinnyTiller](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/10/10003.jpg?1754179816)](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/skinnytiller.10003/)

Looked at a beauty weekend forecast last night and couldn't decide where to fish- another run to Nanticoke or Glasgow. Got text from [@CBS](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/4492/) shortly after and decided to 'even the score' with Glasgow- hooked up the tiller and we were on the road by 7:30am. Launched before 9, right behind a couple gents in a quarter million dollar boat in search of salmon. Right behind us was a couple backing down their 'new to them' boat, on a roller-trailer.... with the winch strap unhooked 🙄 Boat launched itself, barely avoiding landing on the concrete ramp, wife drops the bowline and a runaway boat is now aimed at the tiller 🤨 Didn't see any of it, turned just as [@CBS](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/4492/) made a spectacular grab 💪 to prevent collision.

Beautiful conditions as we headed downhill SE setting up over 45fow- 2 cranks off boards and RRF/Gibbs off Dipsys. 1st fish came on Wonderbread RRF over 57fow then the action stalled so subbed out both boards for Dipsys. Made it ~ halfway to Rondeau before 2nd fish over 67fow. Almost bumped 70fow with no action so turned and headed uphill with bite resuming over 58fow. Kept to 58fow heading E which was the 'zone'. Pulled the pin 'bout 5:15 with decent swell out of the S but still very pleasant.

Very little life on sonar- a few suspended fish or the odd hook hugging bottom. A few worm cleanouts, lost 3 and boated 7 but only came home with 6- one escaped by literally jumping out of the boat! Redfins did most damage- modified Nascar w worm was MVP. Speeds were 2.1-2.4 and Dipsy on 3 with 100' lead produced majority of fish. Water temps consistent ~62°F and conditions were near perfect. Hard to say which was more impressive, the stellar day on the water, or the Central Basin still giving up her 'Gold' this late in the 'post-season' 👌

Pretty much- late Feb to mid-May would be the calender period generally but that schedule is always dependant on water temp. 40-48°F is the sweet spot that usually triggers the spawn. Pretty common for their egg sacs to be 'healthy' now- their feeding and metabolism slow as water cools yet they require large amounts of food (energy) to remain healthy and make those eggs. Have caught the odd one during summer with full egg sac- these don't drop their eggs for some reason and will 'reabsorb' the eggs as protein and then produce another batch for the following spawn.

# Fishing Report - Oct 25. Inner bay yella's and f18s.

Went in search of perch and found a pile of them but not piles of the size I was after. We managed to to get 2¹/² gallons worth of choice ones for our efforts with a couple scoop of minnows.[![20261025\_201847.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73149-f22932259efc76cee1a81afa725f6a9c.jpg?hash=RR0S-OUDYu "20261025_201847.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/20261025_201847-webp.128024/)  
Tossed every spoon, jigging rap, rippin rap and drop shot plastic combo i had on hand but couldn't sell them on the idea of an artificial bait.  
Fresh Lively wiggling minnow was the way to the "keepers" hearts.

# Fishing Report - Are ya sittin down? I went to the pier today :O

So I've been havin a few issues sleepin as is normal for me this time of the year, so I took a sleeping pill last night and slept until just before noon. 😳 I was a little surprised my wife didn't wake me up sooner, but her not doing so let me know when I eventually got up that she didn't have anything planned today. I asked her if she wanted to do anything and she said she couldn't think of anything and I suggested since I didn't have any salted minnows in the freezer and haven't for quite some time, maybe WE go for a ride down to the pier and I see if I can catch any for future use.

She thought about it and said, "no, but you go ahead. We went out yesterday. Besides it gives you something to do and gives me a chance to do things around here without YOU getting in the way while I do it. In fact, take a rod with you because if you get there and see ppl catching fish and don't have one with ya, you'll be pissed and kickin yerself for not taking one." (she knows me well)🤣

So I packed my gear and went to the pier today. 😱 Got there just after 1pm. Stayed until 5:30pm.

Before I left I went next door and let the neighbor know I was going and that IF he decided to make the drive he'd only need a chair as I'd take an extra rod for him just in case. (he never did come down, got busy doing other things)

Picked up some worms just in case and used ONE when I put my line in then started trying for minnows. The one worm was the ONLY worm I used today and it did not induce a bite. 🤷‍♂️ Mixed answers when I asked guys trying for bait how they were faring. One said "a couple here, a couple there", the other said "ain't no minnows." but he was using a smaller minnow net. Once I got mine put together I had NO problem at all catching bait with my 6x6 net. I got some for a friend who was getting there the same time I was as well as getting LOTS for myself. I haz salties again for future use. When that might be, I'm not sure.

Didn't get skunked either. As soon as I replaced the worms on my hooks with minnows, I started getting bites. Didn't catch much, but I did get a nice smallie. Also saw several other nice or nicer smallies caught, one of which was given to me (two came home and eventually made their way to the neighbor) and a few farm animals as well. Despite not seeing or catching any today, I was told by someone I trust to give me accurate info that the walleye are STILL around the pier as at least one was caught on Thursday around 5pm.

All in all a good day. Served its purpose at least. Wanted to catch some bait if I could, and I did, so I'm happy. Catchin a fish, albeit not one I was actively pursuing, was just a bonus. It wouldn't have bothered me had I been skunked tho. I have NEVER fished off the pier this late in the year. I'm normally WELL into hibernation by now, and generally speaking, only one or two people (they know who they are) can get me to come out of hibernation for a day this time of the year.

Haven't decided for sure one way or the other, but I might try again just for something to do sometime next week or I might not. It'll depend on how I feel and how I've been sleeping and of course if the weather cooperates and I don't have anything else planned while my wife is at work. (She was on modified duties last week and off the week before with a sprained knee, work related, but she's back to full duty Monday as her knee has healed enough to allow for that) 🙂
